transcript.text: A dishwasher that 'won't come on' usually points to a power issue first. It could be as simple as a loose plug, a tripped household fuse/RCD, or a control panel lock being active. If the machine is completely dead (no lights at all), please check your electrical supply and ensure the plug is secure. If there are flashing lights or error codes appearing, that will help us identify the specific fault.
No lights at all, totally dead. Everything else in the kitchen works fine and nothing's tripped at the fuse box.

Since the kitchen lights and other appliances are working but the fuse box hasn't tripped, the issue is likely isolated to the dishwasher's power connection or an internal safety component. The most common cause for a 'totally dead' unit in this scenario is that the appliance isn't actually receiving power at its specific plug point (e.g., a loose plug, a switched socket that was turned off, or a faulty extension lead). Please unplug the dishwasher and test the socket with another device, or plug the dishwasher into a different known-working socket to confirm if it has power.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
It's an integrated one, wired in I think, not a normal plug. There's a switch above the worktop and it's on with the little light lit. What next?

Since the main RCD hasn't tripped but the appliance is dead, it is likely the dishwasher is on a dedicated circuit breaker that has tripped independently. This often happens with integrated units because they draw significant current when starting up. Please check your fuse box for any single-switch breakers (often labelled 'Dishwasher' or similar) and ensure one isn't in the off position. If all switches are firmly on, we will need to check if power is actually reaching the switch itself.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
Fuse box has nothing tripped, no separate dishwasher breaker that I can see. Everything's on. What next?

Since the switch is on and nothing has tripped in your main fuse box, the most likely issue is that the switched spur (the unit above the worktop) isn't actually delivering power despite its light being on. Sometimes the indicator lamp works while the internal contacts are burnt or loose. Please toggle the switch off and back on to see if it responds, and ideally test the socket with a small lamp or multimeter to confirm there is live voltage reaching the dishwasher.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
I've already said the switch is on with the light lit. I've no meter or lamp to test it with. Toggling it off and on now, still nothing. Can I check anything else?

The fact that the switch indicator is lit but the dishwasher remains dead suggests the switched spur's internal contacts have failed or burnt out—the small LED often works independently of the high-current terminals. Since you cannot test it yourself right now, please ask a neighbour to plug a small lamp into that socket above the worktop. If the lamp doesn't light up, the spur is faulty and needs replacing by an electrician. If the lamp does work, the issue is likely inside the dishwasher (such as a blown internal mains fuse or control board), which would require an engineer to inspect safely.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
